current.text: Sharpe is expected to start at center for Brooklyn now that Nic Claxton has been traded. Projected starters are Mikel Brown Jr., Egor Demin, Michael Porter Jr., Julius Randle and Sharpe.
Brooklyn signed Mo Wagner. The projected bench has three big men: Wagner, Danny Wolf and Noah Clowney.
Wagner lowers Sharpe's upside, and the experts see a possible messy center split with Wagner and Wolf.
The experts project about 24 minutes a night. The team aims for the mid or high 20s. Getting to 28 minutes is doubtful, and 30 minutes is almost certainly not happening.
When Claxton was out in the past, Sharpe sometimes played very few minutes.
He is on a short two-year contract.

At about 24 minutes he projects as a top 100 category league player, around 80 to 100. At 27 minutes the estimates range from top 50 to 60 up to top 70. If he loses minutes, a pick near Yahoo's rank becomes a bad one.

He is Josh's best category league target. He is underpriced on ESPN. His Yahoo rank is about right for category leagues, and an ADP near 101 is called free real estate. He does not need many minutes to be useful.
Nine-cat rankings will make him look like a top 20 player, and he will not be that.
In a mock auction he went for 10 USD as a starting center, which the buyer still called below his value.
If he does not start early in the season, react right away.
Brooklyn has 16 back-to-backs, tied for the most in the league. With a season that ends March 28, its playoff weeks have 3, 4 and 3 games, with only one back-to-back.
Brooklyn does not own its pick, so it has no reason to tank. It may still give young bigs like Clowney more minutes in the second half, which makes March minutes uncertain.

durable.text: By the numbers he is one of the best offensive rebounders in the league.
He is a per-minute monster who has rarely had the chance to start.
He has improved as a finisher and helps in FG%.
He passes more than most centers and has shown flashes of playmaking. His steals have risen and are high for a center. He has become a versatile defender.
He used to be a shot blocker, but his blocks have been poor lately for unclear reasons.

note: Sharpe is priced like a fringe pick. Yahoo has him at 6 USD (rank 91) and ESPN at 0 USD (rank 136), and nobody drafted him in our league last season. The experts see him as a top 100 category player at 24 minutes, and one mock auction paid 10 USD, so anything up to about 10 USD is a fair bid for a starting center. He helps in REB, STL and FG% and gives nothing in 3PM, with weak FT%. Early in the season, check that he starts and gets at least 24 minutes ahead of Mo Wagner and Danny Wolf.
